 12 weather alerts in effect Sedona flash flood rips out driveways, opens massive sinkholes near Sedona 
 Residents scrambled to escape midday flash floods that left homes damaged and neighborhoods buried in mud. 
 A terrifying rush of floodwater left an Oak Creek Valley neighborhood scarred by mud, debris and a sinkhole just feet from a Sedona-area home. By Mickaela Castillo Published : Nov. 2, 2026 at 8:58 PM MST | Updated : 45 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SEDONA, AZ (AZFamily) — Rapid floodwaters tore through Oak Creek Valley on Sunday afternoon, ripping away entire driveways, opening massive sinkholes, and leaving neighborhoods blanketed in mud and debris just 20 minutes outside downtown Sedona .
 The flash flooding struck in broad daylight around 1 p.m., forcing residents to scramble to evacuate before rushing water cut off escape routes. 
 In some areas, floodwaters reached almost to the windows, and residents stopped mid-evacuation to pull pets from the rising water.
 At one property, the surge carved a massive sinkhole directly in front of a home, tearing away the family’s entire driveway and stopping just feet from the house.
 “It was pretty sad to see this. The road is caved in. Our driveway is caved in,” said homeowner Jera Ramirez, who recorded video of the waters engulfing his property. “I think we took the worst impact out of the entire neighborhood.”
 Across the neighborhood, residents spent Monday assessing extensive structural damage and disrupted basic utilities. 
 However, the threat has not passed: Yavapai County emergency officials have issued another flood alert, keeping the community on alert as cleanup begins.
